# Fact: Project Lifecycle

**Load when:** creating or archiving projects/roles, registering projects in projects.json, or working with the project schema.

## Project creation

**Project IDs:** 6-character random strings using lowercase letters and digits (e.g. `t7r2kn`), generated by `project-init` at creation time and written to `## Project ID` in the project CLAUDE.md. Short enough to be readable, opaque (no rename risk), trivially generated, and unique enough for a small business estate.

**Project type:** Every project has a `type` field — `Ongoing` or `Defined Goal` — stored in the project CLAUDE.md under `## Type` and in `projects.json`. `project-init` prompts for this at creation time. Type is a first-class planning signal: "is this done?" is only meaningful for Defined Goal projects; Ongoing projects never complete, they evolve or get archived.

## Status schema

Five status values — `Active`, `Blocked`, `Completed - Goal Reached`, `Completed - Partial`, `Completed - Abandoned` — consistent across project CLAUDE.md, `projects.json`, and skill prompts. An optional `status_note` string carries free-text context appropriate to the current status: current stage when Active, reason when Blocked, outcome summary when Completed.

## projects.json

`projects.json` lives at `_system/dashboard/data/projects.json` — a flat JSON array, no nesting, no per-role files. Role is a filterable metadata column within each record. Claude never loads it for display — it is consumed by the dashboard SPA directly.

Monday.com holds all Saturn projects. `projects.json` holds only those where Claude has been actively engaged. The gap between the two is the AI adoption signal — a project's absence from the workspace index is meaningful, not an error.

Index maintenance is integrated into existing skills: `project-init` registers a new project on creation; `project-wrap-up` updates `last_worked` at session end. `init-ai-toolkit` does not scaffold `projects.json` at install time — `project-init` creates it as `[]` if absent.

## Role folder structure

Every role folder contains a `_assets/` subfolder for reference material owned by that role and shared across its projects (policies, templates, reference docs that don't belong to any single project). The role CLAUDE.md declares its contents via a `## Role Assets` table — this is how Claude knows to look there without being pointed at it each session.

`role-init` creates the `_assets/` folder and the `## Role Assets` section on role creation. `employee-ai-toolkit-sync` audits for `## Role Assets` in all role CLAUDE.md files.

Three-tier asset model: workspace (`_assets/`) → role (`_assets/`) → project (`_assets/`). The `_` prefix convention applies at all three levels — keeps asset folders sorted above project folders and visually distinct.

## Archive structure

Archives exist at two levels: `_archive/` at workspace root for retired role folders; `[role]/_archive/` for completed projects within a role. A single `archive-project-or-role` skill handles both, detecting target type and routing accordingly.

Board-level company-wide rollout of the AI toolkit is out of scope for this project. This project builds the evidence and assets; the board adoption decision requires a finished evidence base.

## Source decisions

- Project ID format — 6-char alphanumeric (2026-06-16)
- Project type — Ongoing vs Defined Goal (2026-06-16)
- Canonical status values and status_note field (2026-06-17)
- projects.json as project index data layer (2026-06-16)
- Single workspace-level index; role as metadata column (2026-06-16)
- Monday.com is source of truth; workspace index is AI-engaged subset (2026-06-16)
- Index maintenance integrated into existing skills (2026-06-16)
- init-ai-toolkit does not scaffold projects.json (2026-06-16)
- Two-level archive structure (2026-06-16)
- archive-project-or-role skill handles both project and role archiving (2026-06-16)
- Board-level rollout is a separate future project (2026-06-12)
- `_assets/` naming convention (underscore prefix) applies at all three tiers — workspace, role, and project (2026-06-22)
